statement: In a club, every child who plays chess also plays tennis. 8 children play chess, 13 play tennis and 5 play neither. How many children are in the club?

choices.misconception: I took the chess players away from the tennis players as if they had been counted twice, then added the 5.
I counted the tennis players but forgot the children who play neither game.
I added the chess and tennis players, which counts the chess players twice, and forgot the 5.
I added all three numbers, which counts every chess player twice.

hints: Can a child play chess without being one of the tennis players?
Read the first sentence precisely: it puts every chess player inside the tennis group. Draw the chess group as a circle inside the tennis circle.
All 8 chess players are already among the 13 tennis players.

solutions.reliable: Every chess player plays tennis, so the 8 chess players are already counted among the 13 tennis players. Children who play at least one game: 13. Add the 5 who play neither: 13 + 5 = 18. The transferable idea: every A is also B means the A group sits inside B, so it must not be added again.

whyOnTest: Reading 'every chess player also plays tennis' precisely decides how the groups overlap, which is the whole problem.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
